Subject: Consolidating trial credits + pilot pricing question

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile you showed looks promising for our real-time assistant use case. We'd like to run a 6-week pilot with a small internal team (2 engineers + 3 product users) and have a few questions about packaging and whether we can layer promotional credits with a pilot discount.

Specifically:
- Can the $25k startup promo credit be applied up-front to a pilot that also includes a 20% paid pilot discount on Dedicated capacity?
- If we convert to a dedicated reserved commitment at the end of the pilot, can the remaining credit (if any) be applied to the first committed invoice?
- Are there any procurement or SOW requirements we should prepare for?

I've attached a one-pager describing our pilot goals. Happy to hop on a call if that helps.

Best,
Samir Rao
Co-founder & CEO
Hatchworks Labs

Subject: Re: Consolidating trial credits + pilot pricing question

Samir —

Appreciate the one-pager, looks straightforward. Quick answers up front and then a couple of options so we can pick what's operationally simplest: 

Short answers:
- Yes, the startup promo credit can be used during a pilot. We apply credits to usage first before invoicing.
- Remaining promo credit can be applied to the first committed invoice if the conversion happens within 90 days of pilot close (finance requires a documented conversion request).
- For pilots that will convert to Dedicated, we typically use a lightweight SOW + a short addendum to the terms; procurement sometimes requests a PO.

Packaging options (operational notes):
1) Credit-first pilot (simpler): Apply $25k promo credit to all pilot usage. If Hatchworks converts within 90 days, we apply any unused portion to the first invoice. No extra discount on top of credits.
2) Hybrid pilot (recommended for conversion signal): Apply $15k of the promo credit up-front and offer a one-time 15% pilot discount on Dedicated rates for the pilot period. If you convert, we honor the remaining $10k as a one-time credit toward the first committed invoice. This preserves some conversion economics while giving you predictable capacity.
3) Aggressive pilot (requires senior approval): Full $25k + an additional 20% pilot discount for trial window, but the remaining credit is not refundable/transferable — it would be absorbed during pilot. Requires an approval for discount carveout.

Next steps: If option 2 looks good, Marissa can draft a short SOW and Lauren can prepare the conversion clause for finance. Would love to set a 30-min call to confirm timeline.

Pinged Ben from sales ops (cc'd) if there are billing constraints.

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Sales, Startups & GTM
Redwood Inference

Team — looping in sales ops and legal notes. For option 2 (15% pilot discount + split credit), operational checklist below and a proposed SOW outline. I think we can do this as a standard lightweight SOW + conversion addendum.

Operational checklist:
- Approve 15% discount (revenue impact: estimated $3.6k for a 6-week pilot at projected usage) — Ben, please confirm discount cap and whether we need manager sign-off.
- Finance: Reserve the remaining $10k promo credit as "conversion-credit-hold" on HubSpot until conversion or expiry (90d).
- Legal: Simple SOW + conversion addendum template. We need a clause: "Unused promotional credits at pilot close may be applied to the first invoice for a committed reserved contract if conversion is executed within 90 days and Customer requests such application in writing."
- Procurement: Accept Hatchworks PO or provide a statement of work counter with PO acceptance instructions.

Proposed SOW outline (Marissa will draft):
1) Scope & objectives (6-week pilot, teams, success metrics)
2) Services & capacity (Dedicated small pool: 2x A100-equivalent instances; token limits)
3) Pricing & credits (apply $15k promo credit up-front; 15% pilot discount on Dedicated list rates)
4) Conversion path (conversion addendum described above)
5) Termination & data handling

Ben — if you confirm we can price the pilot this way without exec approval, I'll draft the doc and send to Samir. If we need approval, flag it and I'll route.

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. GTM Ops Manager
Redwood Inference
